apples_jimmy.summary: The account has made credible specific calls, including on Claude 4’s timing and capabilities, an xAI o1-style model, and upcoming OpenAI products. Their record is mixed: claims about Gobi, GPT-5, and GPT-4.5 missed, as did a call about Meta’s model weights. Some posts relay information that was already public, and the record is concentrated on OpenAI, so individual claims are best read skeptically.

aibattle_.summary: The account is most dependable on concrete, checkable artifact reports—arena codenames, console strings, model versions, and model-card leaks—with a strong record across labs, especially xAI and several Chinese labs; results on Google are more mixed. Forward-looking release and reveal predictions are less dependable: misses include Nightwhisper, DeepSeek V4 GA, GPT-4.5 Turbo, and Gemini 4 Argon, so timing and speculative claims warrant caution; many posts relay official launch materials or press reports, sometimes with little lead time, and several recent arena-name and model-testing claims remain pending.

haider1.summary: Mainly an aggregator and commentator on OpenAI and Anthropic; much of the output relays reports, company statements, or rumors already public. The account has made strong calls on OpenAI release timing and Kimi K3, but launch-timing claims are mixed, including misses on Gemini 3.5 Pro, Gemini 4 Argon, and OpenAI’s Astra 6.1. Recent claims about Bel, Gemini, Muse, and Aurora remain pending.

tetsuoai.summary: A commentator focused on xAI whose posts mostly relay news that was already public. The account has a credible short-term Grok release-timing call, but missed on detailed feature and pricing roadmaps; a claim about monthly foundation-model releases remains pending. Overall, the record offers limited support for treating the account as an original leak source.

phill__1.summary: The account is strongest on concrete model and release details, with supported calls on Llama 3.1 405B benchmarks, Qwen’s reasoning model with vision, and Gemini 2.0 Flash. The record is small and includes partial as well as mostly accurate calls; some posts relay already-public news, and release timing may be conditional.

iruletheworldmo.summary: The account has made some notable near-term timing calls, including GPT-6's September window and GPT-6 Astra's September 3 release, but its overall record across labs is weak, with OpenAI its comparatively strongest area. They have missed specific dates, specs, and benchmark claims—including on GPT-5.3, Sonnet 5, and an April GPT-6—and also relay unverified rumors; some recorded hits were already public. Recent claims about Google's internal capabilities and an undisclosed demo remain pending.

ns123abc.summary: The account mostly relays already-public reporting, and its settled record is mixed: its calls about Meta hiring and an xAI release were accurate, while its Anthropic Fable timing claim was mostly accurate. It has also made a notable false claim about Trump’s proposed public-partnership framing; recent claims remain unverified.

chrisgpt.summary: The account has made credible OpenAI product and timing calls, including the GPT-6 August target, and its record is strongest on OpenAI; it has also had successful calls on xAI and Anthropic, though results outside OpenAI are based on smaller samples and are more mixed. It has missed Meta model-release predictions and an Anthropic Fable 5.5 claim, and exact timing and other lab-specific predictions can miss; many posts relay already-public reporting, and several recent claims remain pending.

yuchenj_uw.summary: A commentator rather than a dedicated leaker, the account has shown useful OpenAI signal on GPT-5 routing and open-model timing and capabilities, and has made some accurate release-date calls. The settled record is mixed, including misses on specific release predictions; many claims relay information that is already public, and recent claims remain unverified.

alexeheath.summary: The account’s reported claims have held up well so far, including calls on OpenAI ads and Altman’s return talks and Meta’s H1 2026 model plans; no settled misses are recorded. The sample remains limited, some claims were already public, and recent claims about Karpathy joining Anthropic and Anthropic’s appearance at Microsoft’s CEO summit are still pending.

synthwavedd.summary: The account has its strongest record on OpenAI, with well-supported calls on Astra rollout timing and the Opus 5 launch window; its Anthropic calls are more mixed, and its Google record is weak. A notable share of posts relay information already public, and claims about internal codenames or checkpoints can be difficult to verify.

chetaslua.summary: The account combines hands-on model testing with relays of others’ reporting; its settled record is stronger on Google and Zhipu claims, though a Gemini 4 Argon release call missed. Launch calls such as GPT-5.5 and Gemini Spark have largely held up. Overall, the record is mixed: OpenAI claims are less consistent, while Anthropic is a weak spot, with the IPO and AGI predictions among the misses; treat sweeping or longer-range claims cautiously, and note that several recent claims remain pending.

tokengremlin.summary: The account has a generally strong settled record, especially on OpenAI launch timing and rollout signals, including GPT-6 Astra and Sol; its much smaller Anthropic record is mixed, with a notable miss on the predicted near-term Fable 5.5 launch. It has also missed product-structure and timing details, notably saying Luna would launch separately from Sol, and some posts are qualified or inferential. Several recent claims, including claims about OpenAI compute and upcoming developments, remain pending, and some posts summarize official announcements on the day they appear.

scaling01.summary: The account is a fast-moving commentator and relayer rather than a demonstrated insider; many of their calls concern information already public, limiting the evidence of lead time. Their settled record includes accurate near-term release calls for OpenAI and Moonshot, but also misses on claims about Google's training data and purportedly exposed OpenAI API model entries. Broader claims about model scale, internal capability gaps, and timelines remain pending and should be treated cautiously.

dseetharaman.summary: The account's settled record is strongest on OpenAI, with supported Reuters reporting on restructuring tensions and agent-related incidents. The record is narrow and mostly reflects published Reuters reporting, offering limited evidence about advance warning or reliability beyond OpenAI.

btibor91.summary: A prolific, high-signal reverse engineer of the ChatGPT and Claude apps, the account has a strong record, particularly on Anthropic. Its code-level finds have included the ChatGPT image editor, the Aura browser codename, and Claude Code on the web, though some findings take time to ship; a notable share of its posts relay already-public news. Misses include claims about Sora, GPT-5.2-Codex-Max, and a $100 ChatGPT Pro Lite tier, so code references and timing should not be treated as guarantees; many recent findings remain pending.

m1astra.summary: An anonymous app-teardown account focused mainly on OpenAI and Anthropic, with a stronger record on Anthropic and good calls on Claude voice and memory features, as well as OpenAI’s Astra and GPT-Bidi-1. They often identify near-term product work from app or site changes, but also relay already-public material and have missed by over-reading assets or strings, including claims about Sora features and ChatGPT subscription plans. Recent claims remain unsettled.

techdevnotes.summary: An xAI-focused tracker that surfaces product, app, and API traces, though a notable share of its claims are already public and some plans are inferred from those traces. The record includes valid calls, including an OpenAI forecast, but xAI claims have been less reliable, with misses on launch timing and extrapolations about Grok features or model characteristics; evidence of a UI or API presence should not be treated as confirmation of a launch.

aibreakfast.summary: An AI-news aggregator whose settled record is mixed: its strongest listed call was that OpenAI would reveal the GPT-4V API and autonomous agents, while its speculative calls about Gobi, GPT-4.5 Turbo, and o3’s launch-day timing and capabilities missed. The record suggests more caution is warranted with forward-looking claims than with announcement-related coverage, and the settled sample is limited.

xfreeze.summary: The account is an xAI-focused aggregator, and many posts relay public statements or news rather than offer independently verifiable forecasts. Its limited settled record is favorable so far: calls about OpenAI model sizes and Grok Build’s App Deployer feature were confirmed, while recent claims about xAI engineering work and Grok Build features remain pending and unverified.

testingcatalog.summary: The account’s app-code and build-reference findings have often held up, particularly on Anthropic, Google, and Meta; many OpenAI claims have also been credible, though some claims receive only partial support. Many posts relay already-public news, and several recent feature claims remain unverified.

bindureddy.summary: The account often relays circulating rumors and public expectations rather than first-hand leaks, and some credited calls were already public. Their strongest settled results are on OpenAI launch and model calls, with an isolated successful Anthropic call; results are weaker on Google and DeepSeek, while the record does not establish a strength on xAI. Gemini claims about parameters, relative capability, benchmarks, pricing, and latency have been unreliable, and several recent claims remain unresolved.

ai_for_success.summary: An aggregator that mostly reposts news, rumors and official teasers, so much of its output is already public or same-day. Its flags around Gemini Omni and Gemini Spark, along with other Google model developments, have generally been credible but often come with little lead time. Predictive launch-timing calls are less dependable; the record includes a false call that a new version of Jules was close to launching, while a recent Anthropic model claim remains pending.

shiringhaffary.summary: A Bloomberg AI reporter, the account has a strong record on OpenAI funding, restructuring and products, with well-supported reports including Operator, the SoftBank-led funding round and the employee secondary sale. The settled record has no recorded misses, though some calls are rated mostly true rather than fully true, so reported plans or terms may not match the final outcome exactly.

wongmjane.summary: The account has a strong settled record for identifying in-development features, with successful calls across OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Meta; notable examples include ChatGPT file uploads, Bard features, and Advanced Voice on the web. Some posts concern features that were already public, and the Cloudflare–Stripe integration claim was a miss. Recent claims about a Claude avatar creator, Stripe Link balance, and Meta Pay for Muse remain unresolved.

daniel_mac8.summary: The account's overall record is mixed, with a somewhat stronger record on OpenAI than Anthropic. Near-term timing has been a relative strength: GPT-6 Astra's launch day was called exactly, GPT-5.5's timing was broadly right, and Opus 5 was forecast about eight days ahead; longer-range GPT-6 forecasts were repeatedly too early, and the account made false Sonnet 5 launch calls. A substantial share of claims was already public, so originality is a caveat.

kimmonismus.summary: The account is an aggregator that often relays other leakers and public sightings, so many claims are already public by the time they post. Their stronger calls have involved OpenAI releases and access, as well as Grok 4.6; Anthropic calls have been more mixed, including a false claim that Anthropic was ending Haiku. Recent claims about Anthropic’s Fable 5.5, Meta’s Muse Spark 1.4, and an OpenAI agent message board remain unverified.

flowersslop.summary: The account has a mixed track record on OpenAI: calls about GPT-5.5's existence and agent improvements, Images v2's unusually high-resolution generation, and later GPT-6 models have been rated positively. Several near-term release, voice-mode, and AVM predictions have failed, so the account appears more useful for specific model or product leads than for release timing; several recent claims remain unsettled.

kateclarktweets.summary: The account is strongest on explicit financing, valuation, and deal scoops, especially around OpenAI and also Anthropic, with well-supported calls on investor participation and transactions. The supplied record has no outright misses, though some calls are only mostly true and may be imprecise on figures or details; the evidence here concerns business and deal reporting, not model-release leaks.

tomwarren.summary: The account is a Microsoft/Xbox reporter whose concrete claims have generally held up, especially on Microsoft; the settled record has no outright misses, though one claim was only partly accurate. Their record is strongest on Microsoft/Xbox, the Meta sample is limited, and an Xbox disc-to-digital internal-testing claim remains unconfirmed.

imjustnewatai.summary: A high-volume anonymous account whose record is mostly misses: confident dates and elaborate specs for GPT-5, DeepSeek R2 and Grok 5 have failed, though it correctly identified GPT-4.5 as in development. Some OpenAI timing calls, including o4 and ChatGPT-5, have landed, but performance is mixed even on OpenAI claims and weaker on several other labs; quantitative claims such as context windows and prices remain unreliable. Some claims relay already-public news.

vraserx.summary: Mainly an enthusiast amplifier rather than an original source: many posts restate official announcements or other people’s claims, sometimes after the fact. Some broad calls have been supported, including a June window for GPT-5.6, Google Omni, a Codex iOS app, GPT-6 as a new pretraining run, and a possible full-duplex voice mode; exact timing and detailed product or capability rumors have also missed, including the June 11 GPT-5.6 date and Astra. Recent claims remain pending.

amir.summary: The account has a strong, well-supported record on business, funding, and infrastructure scoops, including calls on OpenAI–Amazon financing and compute discussions, Microsoft’s OpenAI partnership, Nvidia’s Blackwell delay, and Anthropic revenue. No settled misses are listed; several recent claims remain pending and are not yet evidence of accuracy.

anissagardizy8.summary: A WSJ infrastructure reporter with a strong record on compute, chips, and funding scoops, including the Blackwell delay, xAI’s planned 100,000-H100 cluster, and Anthropic and Amazon/OpenAI funding news. The settled record has no outright misses, though some calls are only partly confirmed; coverage spans several major AI labs, with especially strong results on OpenAI.

teortaxestex.summary: A DeepSeek- and China-focused commentator, with a sparse record that makes reliability difficult to assess. Concrete calls are mixed: a mostly correct identification of Ox Alpha as GLM-5.3 Flash, alongside false claims that Astra weights had leaked and that DeepSeek would release DSH 0.2 with V4.1 Pro that week.

pankajkumar_dev.summary: An aggregator-style account that posts frequent, detail-heavy leak threads about OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. Broad timing and development claims have often held up, especially for OpenAI; Anthropic has also had successes but some notable misses, while specific Google claims have been less reliable, including the false Snow Bunny report. Much of the account’s material appears to relay public reporting, so codenames, benchmarks, pricing and model attributions warrant caution; its recent Fable 5.5 claims remain unverified.

mark_k.summary: The account makes frequent short-horizon launch calls across AI labs, with well-timed xAI calls, notably Grok 4.5, and some accurate OpenAI calls, including Astra. The overall record is mixed: OpenAI predictions can be directionally right, but specific launch dates and product details have also missed, and many claims are already public when posted.

markgurman.summary: The account has a strong record on Apple strategy, partnerships and product plans, including reporting on Google Gemini’s role in a Siri overhaul, an AI-powered search tool, and Siri features under development; its settled record also includes accurate OpenAI and Meta calls. There are no recorded settled misses, though some calls were only partly accurate; detailed claims about upcoming Apple products remain pending, and the smaller number of calls about other labs offers limited basis for comparison. Some posts reiterate earlier reporting or information that was already public.

steph_palazzolo.summary: The account, an Information AI Agenda reporter, has a strong track record on OpenAI and Anthropic reporting, especially business, funding, and policy; claims are generally right in substance, though some specifics can be partial or change. A notable miss on OpenAI’s planned Sora launch in ChatGPT makes product plans worth treating more cautiously; the Hodge Conjecture claim and several other recent claims remain pending. Many posts promote same-day Information stories, so lead time is often short.

erinkwoo.summary: A tech reporter (formerly The Information, now WSJ) covering Google and OpenAI, with a strong record across a limited sample of specific claims. Verified calls include Google’s Pentagon agreement and Gemini developments, and OpenAI’s Astra preview; the sample also includes near-term forecasts, and some internal details can be difficult to verify independently.

legit_api.summary: The account has a generally solid record on pre-release model details and benchmark claims, with notable calls involving Gemini, GPT-4.5, and Grok; its record is strongest on Google claims and also good on OpenAI and xAI. They are less dependable on precise launch timing and product or API feature predictions, and recent claims about Gemini, OpenAI’s Omni, and Anthropic’s Fable 5.5 remain pending.

andrewcurran_.summary: The account is mainly an aggregator, often relaying major-outlet reporting that is already public rather than offering original leaks. Their near-term release and clearance calls have generally held up, including calls involving Gemini, GPT-Astra, GPT-5.6, GPT-6 Sol, and Spud. More specific speculative claims have been less dependable, with misses on a private-equity venture and Astra’s cyber access; recent claims about internal models and API models remain unresolved.

smokeawayyy.summary: The account makes terse model-and-date calls, sometimes with specific release times, and has a mixed OpenAI record: it correctly called GPT-5 for Aug. 7 and was partly right about ChatGPT memory and a bundle of releases. They have missed speculative claims about GPT-5o and o3-mini timing, and many calls repeat information already public, so their predictions are more informative when they add details not already circulating.

deredleritt3r.summary: The account mostly relays already-public reporting and OpenAI materials, with no verified successful calls in the settled record. Its settled claims that OpenAI had achieved AGI, would separate from Microsoft, would declare AGI in 2025, and would soon release an Olympiad-winning model were false; recent claims about GPT-5.6 Sol Pro, an unreleased internal model, and upcoming large-model launches remain unresolved.

kyliebytes.summary: The account's tracked claims have generally held up, including reports on Anthropic's planned Gulf investment and API-access decision, Meta's hiring and compensation offers, and OpenAI researchers joining Meta. Some posts relay information already public, coverage remains limited, and recent claims are unresolved.
